solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Heading to rowdy parts requires guts (8)

indicatorNotes.Heading to: the heading of a word is what stands at its top, its first letter
indicatorNotes.parts: to part something is to split it, so R forces ENTAILS open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: to entail is to require
first letter of rowdy, placed between ENT and AILS

annotation.surface: A trip to the rough end of town takes nerve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guts' reads as courage in the surface, but here it means innards. 'Parts' is a verb, not a noun meaning districts.
annotation.definitionFit: Guts in the literal, anatomical sense: the bowels and other innards of a body.

entries.clue: One with multiple branches in Kiel malls (3)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is literally in the words that follow, sitting across the gap between them

blocks.note: kiEL Malls

annotation.surface: A shop chain with outlets in the malls of Kiel, the German port.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Multiple branches' suggests a chain store, and the malls help that along; the thing with branches is a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a tree is something with many branches, and the elm is one such tree.

entries.clue: Proceed into snug when darkness has fallen (7)

indicatorNotes.into: going into something means ending up inside it, so ON goes inside TIGHT

blocks.note: a snug fit is a tight one
to go on is to proceed

annotation.surface: Slip into a cosy pub room once it gets dark.
annotation.walkthrough: A snug is also a small cosy room in a British pub, which is the picture the surface paints; here it is the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the answer is the time later today once night has come.

entries.clue: Having knocked off Charlie, now make amends (5)

indicatorNotes.Having knocked off: to knock something off is to strike it away, so the C is struck out

blocks.note: at once = now
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet; it is removed

annotation.surface: Someone who has killed a man called Charlie must now make up for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked off' reads as murdered, which is why amends are needed; it only removes a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: making up for a wrong is what the answer means, often with a religious flavour.

entries.clue: Light service after delayed train finally got in (7)

indicatorNotes.after: one thing after another in a sentence becomes one after the other in the answer, so RN follows
indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so the last letter of train
indicatorNotes.got in: getting in means entering, so N enters LATE

blocks.note: a delayed train is late
last letter of train, placed inside LATE
RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

annotation.surface: A skeleton rail service runs after the delayed train finally arrived.
annotation.walkthrough: Commuter words everywhere, but 'service' is the Navy and 'Light' is a noun, a lamp.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a lantern is one kind of light, a lamp with a case you can carry.

entries.clue: Long whiskers needing bit off the top (4)

indicatorNotes.needing bit off the top: a trim off the top takes away the start, and in an across answer the start is the first letter

blocks.note: 'tache is short for moustache; the T comes off

annotation.surface: A long moustache wants a trim at the top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long whiskers' reads as one phrase, but 'Long' is the verb, to yearn.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym of the verb: to long for something and to ache for it are the same yearning.

entries.clue: Honesty is able to provide you with armour ultimately (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of armour is used

blocks.note: can = is able to
to do lunch is to provide it
U = you, text-speak
last letter of armour

annotation.surface: Being honest is the best protection you have.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a proverb about honesty as armour. 'Provide' for DO is the catering sense: a pub that does food provides it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: candour is frankness, the habit of saying honestly what you think.

entries.clue: Operatic man travelling about Lincoln? (11)

indicatorNotes.travelling about: something travelling about moves all over the place, and so do the letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: An opera singer on tour around the English city of Lincoln.
annotation.walkthrough: Lincoln is a city in England, which suits a touring singer, but the question mark points to Abraham Lincoln, called the Great Emancipator for ending slavery in the US.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: Abraham Lincoln is the best-known emancipator, freer of the slaves.

entries.clue: State being led by opinionated leader (4)

indicatorNotes.led by: whatever leads goes in front, so O comes before MAN
indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of a word is the letter at its head, its first

blocks.note: first letter of opinionated
a man is a (human) being

annotation.surface: A country run by a stubborn ruler.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' could be a verb, to say something; it is the country.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Oman is one sovereign state, on the Arabian Peninsula.

entries.clue: Ant-Man role to be recast for show (10)

indicatorNotes.to be recast: to recast is to cast again in a new shape, so the letters are remoulded

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: The superhero part is being given to a new actor for the film.
annotation.walkthrough: Ant-Man is a Marvel superhero, and recasting is film talk; 'show' seems to be the production, not a display.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrase synonym: something decorative rather than useful is there for show.

entries.clue: Contrary bishop about to punch drug king (7)

indicatorNotes.Contrary: contrary means facing the opposite way, so B and CA are turned round
indicatorNotes.to punch: a punch drives into something, so ACB is driven into METH

blocks.note: B = bishop in chess
ca. = circa, about; B+CA turned round gives ACB
meth = methamphetamine; ACB goes in after the M

annotation.surface: A wayward cleric is about to hit a drug lord.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drug king' reads as a kingpin, but 'king' alone is the definition: Shakespeare's Scottish king.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Macbeth was an eleventh-century king of Scotland, and Shakespeare's tragic one.

entries.clue: I pressure a revolutionary to seize English crown (6)

indicatorNotes.revolutionary: a revolution is a turn right round, so the letters come back reversed
indicatorNotes.to seize: seizing something means grabbing it and holding it, so the reversed letters take E inside

blocks.note: ego is Latin for I, and the self
P = pressure in physics
EGO+P+A turned round gives APOGE
E = English; it goes in before the last letter

annotation.surface: Someone leans on a rebel to take the English throne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun, a rebel; it is the instruction to turn EGO, P and A round.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: the apogee is a culmination or high point, as a crown is the top of something.

entries.clue: Stapler could be something used to treat major injuries (7,4)

annotation.definition: something used to treat major injuries

blocks.note: the answer is the instruction: PLASTER is STAPLER cast, that is with its letters rearranged

blocks.clueFragment: something used to treat major injuries
blocks.note: the definition of the whole answer

annotation.surface: An office stapler could be used for patching up badly hurt people.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read as wordplay, the answer says 'plaster = stapler, cast', and cast is an anagram word. A plaster cast holds a broken bone still.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a plaster cast is the hard shell set round a broken limb, so it treats a serious injury.

entries.clue: Invade someone’s space or chance going around? (8)

indicatorNotes.going around?: something going around circulates and changes position, so the letters shift about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Do you step into someone's personal space, or just risk wandering about?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chance' seems a verb meaning risk; it is just letters to shuffle with OR.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrase synonym: to encroach is to intrude gradually on ground that belongs to someone else.

entries.clue: Support given to old fellow and old vegetarian (8)

indicatorNotes.given to: a thing given to another is joined to it, so MAST is attached to the front of O and DON

blocks.note: a mast supports a sail or aerial
O = old
a don is a fellow of a college

annotation.surface: Help is given to an elderly man and an elderly vegetarian.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old vegetarian' sounds like a pensioner off meat; the mastodon was an extinct plant-eating relative of the elephant.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful description: the mastodon is long extinct, so old, and it ate only plants.

entries.clue: Note delivered after the last month in fall (7)

indicatorNotes.delivered after: a note delivered after something arrives later, so LINE comes after DEC

blocks.note: Dec is the short form of December
a line is a short letter, as in drop me a line

annotation.surface: A letter arrived at the end of the year, in autumn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fall' reads as the American autumn next to 'month', but it is a noun meaning a drop.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fall in prices or health is a decline.

entries.clue: Nurse and artist getting pint will be delighted (6)

indicatorNotes.getting: getting something means acquiring it, so EN and RA acquire PT on the end

blocks.note: EN = enrolled nurse
RA = Royal Academician, an artist
pt = pint

annotation.surface: A nurse and a painter will be happy to get a pint.
annotation.walkthrough: The pint here is only its abbreviation, not a drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be carried away with joy is to be enraptured, a rarer form of the same word.

entries.clue: Cat starts to inhale catnip after a minute (6)

indicatorNotes.starts to: the starts of words are their opening letters, so I and C
indicatorNotes.after: the cat and its letters come after the A

blocks.note: the a is used as it stands
a tom is a male cat
first letters of inhale and catnip

annotation.surface: A cat takes a sniff of catnip in no time at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A minute' reads as a spell of time, but 'minute' is the adjective, pronounced my-NEWT, and the 'a' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: anything on the scale of atoms is minute, extremely small.

entries.clue: Shock about mutually assured destruction created by US (3-4)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so MANE wraps round MAD

blocks.note: a shock of hair is a mane
MAD is the Cold War acronym

annotation.surface: Alarm about the nuclear arms doctrine of the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: The capitals make it the USA, but read as 'us' it is people: made by humans.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: anything man-made was produced by human beings, that is by us.

entries.clue: We don’t believe volunteers rejected jobs (8)

indicatorNotes.rejected: something rejected is thrown back, so TA comes back to front

blocks.note: TA = Territorial Army, volunteer soldiers; turned round to AT
a job is criminal slang for a robbery

annotation.surface: Staff doubt the rejected volunteers were ever doing real work.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the answer: atheists would say 'we don't believe'. The TA is Britain's former volunteer army reserve.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition in the answer's own voice: what the group itself would say about God.

entries.clue: Fish waiters finally sell in French city (7)

indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of sell
indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so L sits within ANGERS

blocks.note: Angers is a city in western France
last letter of sell

annotation.surface: Restaurant staff at last sell fish in a French town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fish waiters' looks like staff who serve fish; anglers are those who wait for the fish to bite.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: anglers sit waiting for fish, so they are fish waiters.

entries.clue: People soon to take on husband (7)

indicatorNotes.to take on: taking something on means taking it aboard, so IN A BIT takes H inside

blocks.note: in a bit = soon
h = husband; it goes after IN

annotation.surface: Folk will be taking on a husband before long.
annotation.walkthrough: 'People' is a verb here: to people a place is to fill it with inhabitants.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym: settlers who people a land come to live there.

entries.clue: Endlessly oppressive row … good call to stop it (8)

indicatorNotes.to stop: to stop a hole is to plug it, so DIN plugs RING

blocks.note: g = good
to give someone a ring is to call them
a row is a din, a racket; it goes inside RING

annotation.surface: A tiresome argument keeps going until someone phones to end it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with cow here, a noise; the clue puts it before the call it goes into.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: grinding poverty or toil is relentless and wearing, oppressive with no end.

entries.clue: City abroad learning about a bit of history (6)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so LORE goes round A and H
indicatorNotes.a bit of: a bit is a small piece, here just the first letter of history

blocks.note: lore is learning, knowledge
the a is used as it stands
first letter of history

annotation.surface: Studying overseas teaches you a little history.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface, as in 'a bit of history', but in the wordplay it is a letter of its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Lahore is a city in Pakistan, abroad from a British point of view.

entries.clue: Drunk spends billions in game of chance (5)

indicatorNotes.spends: what you spend is gone, so the B is used up and removed

blocks.note: blotto is slang for very drunk
b = billion; it is removed

annotation.surface: A drunk blows a fortune gambling.
annotation.walkthrough: Blotto is British slang for very drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: lotto, a lottery or bingo-like draw, is one game of chance.

entries.clue: Board game Manet invented featuring Newton (10)

indicatorNotes.invented: something invented is made up anew, so the letters are made into a new word
indicatorNotes.featuring: featuring means including, so N is included in the mix

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
N = newton, the unit of force

annotation.surface: A board game the painter Manet came up with, with Isaac Newton in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Board game' reads as one phrase, but 'Board' alone is the definition, and Newton is only the unit letter N.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the business sense: the directors who run a company.

entries.clue: Sweetheart of sailor appearing in Times (4)

indicatorNotes.appearing in: to appear in something is to be seen within it, so AB sits inside BY

blocks.note: 3 by 4 means 3 times 4
AB = able seaman

annotation.surface: A sailor's girlfriend makes the newspaper.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes it the newspaper, but times is multiplication, as in 'by'.
annotation.definitionFit: A term of endearment: baby and sweetheart are both pet names for a loved one.

entries.clue: What people are usually in when they’re out? (3)

annotation.definition: What people are usually in when they’re out?

blocks.note: a place people are inside
out means out cold, asleep, not away from home

annotation.surface: A riddle about where people are when they are not at home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out' seems to mean away from home; it means out cold, asleep, and sleepers are in bed.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: people who are out for the count are usually lying in bed.

entries.clue: One earl dons heartlessly told to get knotted (4)

indicatorNotes.dons: to don is to put on, as clothes, so TD is put on round I and E
indicatorNotes.heartlessly: without a heart means without the middle, so OL goes from told

blocks.note: told without its heart (OL)
I = one, the Roman numeral
E = earl; I and E go inside TD

annotation.surface: A nobleman puts on clothes and is told, unkindly, to get lost.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get knotted' is British slang for go away; here 'knotted' simply means fastened with a knot.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a knotted rope is a tied one.

entries.clue: Various first-class or tedious shows (8)

indicatorNotes.shows: to show something is to let it be seen, and the answer can be seen inside the words

blocks.note: first-clASS OR TEDious

annotation.surface: A range of programmes, some excellent, some dull.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shows' looks like television programmes, and the surface makes them a mixed bag, but it says the answer is on display.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an assorted selection is a various one, of many kinds.
